title: Workflow-Backed SMS Verification for Anonymous Rock Forms
distilled_summary: A reusable optional-verification pattern for anonymous Rock forms: require one exact person match before sending an SMS code, persist a bounded challenge in a dedicated workflow, never expose the matched alias to the browser, and atomically consume the verified challenge on the server immediately before the intended action.

recipe.title: Workflow-Backed SMS Verification for Anonymous Rock Forms
recipe.summary: Optionally recognize an existing person during an anonymous Rock form using an exact unique match, persisted workflow challenge, bounded SMS code, and single-use server-side final recheck.
use_cases: Optionally recognize a returning person during an anonymous registration or request form.
Prefill or associate a final form action only after phone-possession verification.
Keep short-lived verification state server-side without trusting browser-provided person identifiers.
outcomes: Only one exact eligible person match can receive a challenge.
The browser receives an opaque challenge session but no person or alias identifier.
A verified challenge is bound to one intended action, expires, counts attempts, and can be consumed only once.
prerequisites: A dedicated Rock workflow type with the attributes and SMS delivery actions documented by the package.
A configured SMS transport and an explicit communication-history retention decision.
Permission to create secured Helix Lava Application POST endpoints and anonymous abuse controls.
A privacy and risk review for the form data used in exact matching.

adaptation_points.description: Set the GUID of the dedicated verification workflow type after creating and reviewing its attributes and actions.
adaptation_points.example: Use a local workflow type GUID; the recipe provides no default.

adaptation_points.description: Choose a stable local action key that prevents a verified challenge from being reused on another form or operation.
adaptation_points.example: Use a non-secret application-specific key such as volunteer-application-submit.

adaptation_points.description: Set the local DefinedValue ID used for mobile phone numbers and verify that messaging-enabled semantics match the target instance.
adaptation_points.example: Use the target instance value; the recipe intentionally uses zero as an invalid placeholder.

adaptation_points.description: Review first/nickname, last name, email, mobile number, messaging-enabled state, and birthdate as an exact-match policy appropriate for the form risk.
Set expiration, verification attempts, per-person sends, per-source sends, and upstream anonymous traffic controls.
adaptation_points.example: The public defaults cap expiration at ten minutes and page-level attempts at five, but local risk may require stricter controls.

adaptation_points.description: Configure POST-only endpoint security, anti-CSRF behavior, TLS, monitoring, and staff-only access to workflow or communication review surfaces.

security.authentication: Anonymous form request plus possession of the SMS destination; this is not account authentication or identity proofing.
security.authorization: The challenge may authorize only its configured intended form action; workflow and communication administration remain restricted to appropriate staff roles.
notes: Zero or multiple person matches fail closed, and every start response uses the same browser-visible shape.
The browser never receives the matched person ID, alias ID, or alias GUID.
The final endpoint rechecks expiration, verification, intended action, and single-use consumption on the server.
A six-digit code hash reduces accidental exposure but does not resist an attacker who can read the database; database controls, rate limits, expiration, and retention remain required.
SMS is vulnerable to interception and redirection and must not be described as strong identity proofing or phishing-resistant MFA.
The originating implementation informed this rewrite, but the hardened public package requires live verification in each target instance.
Verify Lava transaction behavior, WorkflowActivate attribute keys, SQL Server CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM support, endpoint CSRF behavior, proxy-aware client IP handling, and SMS retention before launch.
The package was reviewed against the Rock 17/18 model family.

files.purpose: Adaptation, security boundary, validation, and compatibility guidance
Public-safe application rigging with invalid placeholders and bounded defaults
Persisted workflow attribute and activation-action contract
Exact unique match, rate limiting, random code, and challenge activation reference
Atomic attempt counting and server-side code verification reference
Single-use final challenge consumption and server-only person resolution reference

instructions: Review the immutable README, workflow contract, source, and static test before adapting the recipe.
Create a dedicated verification workflow and configure its SMS action to clear the plain Code attribute immediately after delivery.
Create POST-only start, check, and final-submit endpoints with only the required Lava commands and anti-CSRF behavior.
Supply every local configuration value without introducing fallback production IDs or routes.
Integrate the final-submit recheck immediately before the protected form action and use only its server-resolved alias context.
Add anonymous traffic controls, monitoring, retention decisions, privacy review, and an accessible non-SMS path before launch.
validation_steps: Run python3 tests/static_contract.py from the recipe directory.
Confirm one exact eligible match sends one code while zero or multiple matches send none.
Confirm all start responses have the same status, message, timing envelope where practical, and field shape.
Confirm invalid, expired, over-attempt, wrong-action, already-verified, and consumed challenges fail safely.
Race two final submissions and confirm only one can consume the challenge.
Inspect browser responses and confirm no person ID, alias ID, or alias GUID is present.
Confirm per-person, per-source, resend, and upstream anonymous traffic limits work through the real proxy path.
Confirm the plain Code workflow value is cleared and review any rendered SMS retained in communication history.
Confirm the protected final action cannot run by submitting only browser fields without a valid server-side challenge.
rollback_steps: Disable the three Lava Application endpoints and remove their page/form integration.
Deactivate the verification workflow type or its SMS action to stop new messages.
Revert the protected form to its non-verified anonymous path; existing verification workflow rows can expire under the approved retention policy.
known_limitations: SMS possession is not complete identity proofing, account authentication, or phishing-resistant MFA.
The public package is a reference integration and has not been live-tested unchanged in a generic Rock instance.
Exact match fields can exclude legitimate people with stale or shared data and require an accessible fallback.
Context.Request.UserHostAddress may identify a reverse proxy unless the target environment provides a trusted client-address mechanism.
Consuming before a downstream action means a downstream failure requires a new challenge; combine operations transactionally if the local implementation can do so safely.
learnings: Treat anonymous recognition as a persisted, bounded server challenge rather than as a browser state transition.
Fail closed on ambiguous person matches instead of selecting the oldest or lowest-ID candidate.
Return an opaque session for every start request so browser response structure does not reveal whether a person exists.
Never let a browser-supplied person or alias identifier establish verified applicant context.
Bind each challenge to an intended action, enforce expiration and attempt limits, and consume it exactly once at final submission.
Separate the short-lived delivery code from durable audit state and make communication retention an explicit decision.

title: Communication History Active Search
distilled_summary: A reusable read-only Helix Lava Application pattern that separates the filter shell from the results endpoint, allowlists communication enums and page sizes, parameterizes text search, pages before calculating recipient aggregates, and keeps message bodies and recipient-level details out of the initial staff view.

recipe.title: Communication History Active Search
recipe.summary: Build a secured read-only Helix communication browser with allowlisted filters, parameterized search, bounded pagination, and aggregate recipient outcomes.
use_cases: Give authorized staff a responsive communication history browser without loading a full page after every filter change.
Filter communications by Rock status, communication type, subject or name, and bounded pages.
Review aggregate delivery outcomes without exposing message bodies or recipient-level contact information.
outcomes: Filter changes replace only the result table and pager through HTMX.
All user text reaches SQL through parameters and enum values are allowlisted.
Recipient aggregation is bounded to the selected page of communications.
prerequisites: Permission to create and secure a Helix Lava Application and Rock page.
A staff role authorized to view communication history.
A local communication detail page if record links are enabled.
A representative communication dataset for query-plan and aggregate validation.

adaptation_points.description: Choose all, draft, pending approval, approved, or denied for the initial view.
Choose a bounded initial page size of 25, 50, or 100.
Set a locally authorized communication detail page or leave zero to render no record links.
adaptation_points.example: Use a local numeric page ID; the public recipe provides no working default.

adaptation_points.description: Update both relative Helix endpoint routes if the application slug differs from the recipe default.
Restrict the Rock page and both endpoints to authenticated staff roles permitted to view communication activity and outcomes.

security.authorization: ApplicationView and page permissions limited to approved communication-history roles
notes: The public reference excludes message bodies, SMS text, recipient names, addresses, phone numbers, and recipient-level errors.
Communication names, schedules, senders, and delivery aggregates remain sensitive staff data.
The results endpoint uses GET only for read behavior and caps requests at 100 rows.
Approval, resend, cancel, delete, and other writes require separate endpoints, authorization, CSRF protection, validation, auditing, and rollback.
Verify the Communication and CommunicationRecipient enum and field behavior against the target Rock release.
Performance depends on communication volume, database indexes, search selectivity, and recipient counts.
The model map identifies communication status 3 as Approved; it must not be relabeled as Sent.

files.purpose: Deployment, security, validation, and compatibility guidance
Public-safe defaults and invalid local detail-page placeholder
Filter shell, HTMX state, and initial endpoint rendering
Parameterized query, bounded pagination, status mapping, and aggregate result rendering

instructions: Review the pinned README, source, configuration, and static test at the immutable commit.
Create secured GET list and results endpoints and enable Sql only on the results endpoint.
Set local default filters, page size, optional detail page, and relative endpoint routes without introducing production defaults.
Render the list endpoint inside a Lava Application Content block on a staff-only Rock page.
Preserve parameterized text search, enum allowlists, the 100-row cap, and the exclusion of message and recipient details.
Test query plans and response times with realistic communication and recipient volume.
validation_steps: Run python3 tests/static_contract.py from the recipe directory.
Confirm unauthenticated and unauthorized users cannot load the page or either endpoint.
Confirm status 3 displays Approved rather than Sent.
Confirm status, type, text, and page-size changes reset pagination to page one.
Submit quotes, percent characters, underscores, and brackets as search text and confirm they cannot change SQL statement structure.
Confirm invalid status and type values fall back to all and invalid page sizes fall back to 25.
Confirm no request can return more than 100 rows.
Compare aggregate recipient counts with known communications and confirm transient rows and message bodies are absent.
Confirm empty results and first, middle, and last pagination states render correctly.
rollback_steps: Disable or remove the Lava Application endpoints and page block.
Restore the previous communication-history page configuration; no data rollback is required because the recipe performs only reads.
known_limitations: Subject and name search uses SQL LIKE and may require a different index or search strategy on very large datasets.
The result count and page query are separate reads and may differ briefly while communications change concurrently.
The recipe reports aggregate recipient statuses but does not reproduce every official communication analytics feature.
The reference UI is intentionally minimal and should be adapted to the organization's design system without weakening filter or authorization boundaries.
learnings: Separate the filter shell from the results endpoint so HTMX updates only the changing region.
Allowlist status, type, and page-size values and bind free text as SQL parameters instead of interpolating sanitized strings.
Page communication rows before running correlated recipient aggregates so cost scales with the visible page.
Use the Rock enum name Approved for status 3 and show send and delivery evidence separately.
Keep the initial operational view narrow and require explicit review before adding message bodies or recipient-level data.
A read-only endpoint still needs application and page authorization because communication activity is sensitive.
